answer: A lantern-lit registry can resist sybils by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake bond before it may transact: the bond acts like a velvet rope, letting one verified identity through while duplicate accounts must each pay the same lock-up. If peers detect two identities controlled by one operator, the bond is slashed and the identities burned. An attacker who wants to wander the market with a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand bonds, while an honest agent pays only one refundable deposit and earns it back by behaving well.
